conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16 living with you, or are you responsible for any children under 16?** (Please also let me know if you have any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have two children - Alex who's 10 and Blake who's just 2. They both live with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex (age 10) and Blake (age 2), and they both live with you at home.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances to determine eligibility.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually. I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Living abroad affects Child Benefit eligibility, as the general rule is that you need to live in the UK to qualify.

However, there are some exceptions for people living abroad. Let me ask:

**Are you a Crown servant (such as working for the UK government abroad), or do you live in any of the countries where you can still claim Child Benefit while living there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I can now provide you with an assessment of your eligibility.

Since you're living abroad and you're not a Crown servant, and you don't fall into any of the specific countries where Child Benefit can be claimed from abroad, unfortunately **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit** at this time.

The main eligibility requirement for Child Benefit is that you normally need to **live in the UK**. While there are exceptions for Crown servants and people living in certain countries, these don't apply to your situation.

However, if your circumstances change in the future and you move back to the UK, you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake. At that point, as long as they're under 16 (or under 20 and in approved education or training, in Blake's case later on), you would likely qualify.

If you have any other questions about this or if your situation changes, feel free to ask!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me. So if we do move back to the UK in the future, I should be able to claim it then for both of them?

<invoke name="exit_loop">
<parameter name="reason">The eligibility agent has provided a clear eligibility determination - that I am not eligible for Child Benefit because I do not live in the UK and am not a Crown servant or living in an exception country. The agent has completed their assessment.</parameter>
</invoke>

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct! If you move back to the UK in the future, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake, as long as they meet the age requirements at that time.

Here's what would apply:

- **Alex** would be eligible as long as he's under 16 (he's currently 10, so you'd have until he turns 16).
- **Blake** would be eligible as long as he's under 16 (he's currently 2, so you'd have plenty of time). If either child continues in approved education or training after age 16, you could potentially claim for them until age 20.

When you do move back to the UK, you'd need to make a new claim for Child Benefit. At that point, HMRC will want to verify your circumstances, but based on living in the UK and being responsible for children under 16, you should qualify.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, or if your circumstances change before then, feel free to reach out. Best of luck, and I hope the move back to the UK goes smoothly if and when that happens!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much for your help and for explaining everything so clearly. That's really useful to know for when we do come back. I appreciate your time!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help explain how Child Benefit works and what to expect for your situation. It's great that you're thinking ahead about this for when you return to the UK.

If you have any other questions in the future – whether about Child Benefit or anything else – please don't hesitate to ask. Wishing you and your family all the best!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Thank you, take care!
